capabilities: Shift through four color phases computed from local sunrise and sunset
Apply tile motifs, serif fonts and card-like styling to titles, callouts, tables and tags
Render Reading view as a printed page with margin footnotes, drop caps and fading sidebars
Show time, date, weather and recent notes on a new empty tab
Provide a sample page and three note templates (Book, Long-read, Daily)
extras: Desktop only; untested on phones and tablets. Weather uses Open-Meteo over the network (geocoding and forecast, at most every 30 minutes); setting Weather to Off stops all fetches, and sunrise/sunset are computed locally. Looks best on Obsidian's default theme; results on other themes depend on the theme.
motivation: The author built it for their own vault and separated the look from their notes so it works in any vault.
problem: Obsidian themes use a single static look, so nothing changes the vault's appearance with the time of day or gives notes a printed-page reading style.

relations.evidence: both go to Open-Meteo, a free weather service that needs no account or key

summary: Theme that dresses Obsidian in Persian tilework, with palettes that shift through four phases set by local sunrise and sunset, serif type and a book-like reading view.
